title: controlplane-rota-sync-raw-notes-2026-05-12
content:
Attendees: Ava (owner), Marcus (routing), Priya (auth), Liam (quotas), Sofia (SRE cover), plus floating: Jeff (infra) joined 10m in.

Purpose: weekly rota sync — capture oncall handoff notes, outstanding investigations, planned canaries, and short action items rather than long PR summaries. Raw, rough; will push clean minutes to Confluence if needed.

1) Incident recap (May 10, 03:22 UTC) — short
- Symptoms: brief spike in 503s from hosted API. Affected path: /v1/generate routed via us-west primary.
- Root cause (current hypothesis): routing table sharding mismatch after autoscaler churn — some requests hit a stale route entry that pointed to drained pool; fallback path overloaded.
- Mitigation applied: SRE (Sofia) increased conservative routing TTL to 60s and temporarily disabled the aggressive drain policy (INF-4321). Error budget sliding window returned to normal in ~12m.
- Open: need a deterministic test for route-shard reconciliation (see action items).

2) Routing workstream updates
- Marcus: completed first pass of the canary for adaptive-routing based on seq_len distribution. Canary target: 5% traffic for low-latency tier starting Wed. Plan: run for 48h, monitor p95 and error rate.
  - Metrics to watch: p50/p95 latency, 4xx/5xx ratio, queue depth, token throughput.
  - Note: add a Canary rollback hook that can automatically cut traffic if p95 > baseline+40% or error_rate > 0.5%.
- Action: Marcus to draft canary playbook and add thresholds to the rollout config (linked INF-4410). Owner: Marcus. ETA: 2026-05-15.

3) Auth/token rotation & header bloat (Priya)
- Repro: some internal customers hit auth failures when JWT size exceeded 8KB leading to downstream gateway 400s. Root cause: multiple optional claims (debug:request_id, deployment_tag) appended by service mesh.
- Short term: Priya pushed a patch to strip nonessential claims at ingress and return structured error (PR #2123).
- Medium term: revamp token claim policy and consider reference token flow for large sessions.
- TODO: create RFC for "lightweight session tokens" — Priya + Security to draft by 2026-05-21.

4) Quotas & throttling adjustments (Liam)
- Observed client churn when quota enforcement moved from token-bucket to leaky-bucket in staging. Some customers saw a transient drop in throughput.
- Decision: revert to token-bucket with dynamic refill in the short term; evaluate hybrid algorithm for bursty workloads.
- Action: Liam to run load sims (synth traffic: short bursts, long-tail) and share results in next sync. Linked artifacts: test plan in internal spreadsheet (ref in Slack). ETA: 2026-05-18.

5) Control plane: reconciliation tests and idempotency
- Problem: control-plane reconcile loop doesn't always detect ephemeral route metadata drift during reschedule. This is the likely factor in the May 10 incident.
- Proposal: add a versioned route-hash and include last-applied annotation with checksum — reconcile should compare checksums rather than blind apply.
- Cost: small CPU and storage footprint; benefits: faster detection of divergence.
- Decision: proceed with experiment in staging. Owner: Ava + Jeff. ETA for staging rollout: 2026-05-20.

6) Oncall handoff notes (for next week)
- Week coverage: May 17–23: primary oncall = Marcus, secondary = Priya.
- Handoff items: watch for canary alert set (Marcus), monitor token error spikes (Priya), and be ready to toggle routing TTL if cluster eviction events observed.
- Quick checklist for handoff:
  - Confirm active deploys in prod via /deployments dashboard.
  - Verify routing TTL and drain policy config.
  - Ensure quota sim is running by EOD Monday.

7) Low-urgency backlog (notes to self)
- Replace freeform 'notes' logger with typed audit events so we can query by reason for each route update. (nice-to-have)
- Investigate using an external config diff tool (e.g., ArgoCD hooks) to preview route changes before apply.
- Revisit the SLA language around graceful-degrade strategies for Dedicated customers.

8) Risks and decisions
- Risk: canary could temporarily raise p95 for larger models if batching changes — mitigation is small traffic slice and fast rollback.
- Decision: do not change drain policy until we have route-shard reconciliation tests passing.

9) Action items (concise)
- Marcus: Canary playbook + rollout thresholds (INF-4410). ETA 2026-05-15.
- Priya: RFC for lightweight session tokens + patch followups (PR #2123). ETA 2026-05-21.
- Liam: quota load sims and results posting. ETA 2026-05-18.
- Ava & Jeff: staging rollout for route-hash reconciliation experiment. ETA 2026-05-20.
- Sofia: retro writeup for May 10 incident with timeline and PagerDuty links. ETA 2026-05-16.

10) Misc notes / links (raw)
- Slack thread: #platform-controlplane (see thread pinned messages)
- Playbook draft: Control Plane Playbook (Confluence) — will synth into the 'canary playbook' later.
- Related JIRAs: INF-4321 (incident), INF-4387 (auth header patch), INF-4410 (routing canary).

Closing: raw notes — please add any missed items. If you spot something urgent (alerts firing) ping oncall directly and add to INF-4321 timeline.

----END RAW----

(Notes to self: convert this to cleaner minutes and push to /confluence/platform/control-plane-weekly. Remove the raw Slack links and squash duplicate references.)
